messages:
mara: Hey team — escalation from ACME EU customer. Since ~08:00UTC they're seeing 5-10s tail latencies and intermittent 503s for text-generation calls. They say requests are landing in us-west rather than eu-central. Billing spike from egressto-us-west observed. Can someone triage?

devin: @mara can you paste one of the failing request IDs or a sample curl? Also which gateway version are they on?

mara: sample request id: req_20260317_8f7b. curl: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` — response headers show `x-handled-region: us-west-2` and `x-auth-path: /auth/external` even though customer is in eu-central-1.

sre-alex: Noted. @devin any recent rollout touching the L7 proxy or header rewrite filters?

devin: We rolled a canary of `gateway-proxy:v3.12.0` at 07:45UTC which included the new L7 header-merge filter to reduce header bloat. It was supposed to preserve `x-region-hint` but maybe we broke the merge order. ops-bot, can you show the rollout events?

ops-bot: rollout event: gateway-proxy:v3.12.0 canary -> 10% -> started 2026-03-17T07:45:00Z. No automated rollback triggered.

mara: The customer repro steps: 1) from an EU client, 2) POST to /v1/generate, 3) observe 503s and `x-handled-region` header set to `us-west-2`. They repro reliably by hammering with 20 concurrent short requests.

sre-alex: Can you grab the proxy logs for req_20260317_8f7b? Look for any header rewrite traces and upstream selection logs (envoy -> cluster selection).

mara: paste of relevant proxy log lines (redacted):
```
[2026-03-17T07:59:12.123Z] incoming: src=10.4.2.11, host=api.redwood.ai, headers={:method=POST, :path=/v1/generate, :authority=api.redwood.ai, x-region-hint=eu-central-1, authorization=Bearer REDACTED}
[2026-03-17T07:59:12.124Z] header-merge-filter: original x-region-hint=eu-central-1, preserved-x-region-hint=, merged-x-region-hint=us-west-2
[2026-03-17T07:59:12.125Z] cluster_select: selected cluster=redwood-eu-fallback->redwood-us-west-01
[2026-03-17T07:59:12.126Z] upstream response: 503 Service Unavailable (upstream connect error)
```

sre-alex: That second line looks exactly like the header-merge bug. merged-x-region-hint should not be us-west-2 if incoming x-region-hint=eu-central-1. I suspect the merge filter falls back to the first element from an internal list of preferred regions but we are reading from the wrong vector.

devin: I can repro locally with the canary config. Minimal repro: run envoy with the header-merge filter and send two headers: `x-region-hint: eu-central-1` and `x-proxy-region: us-west-2` (internal). The filter currently prefers `x-proxy-region` when present even if `x-region-hint` is set by client. That explains the wrong selection.

mara: So for affected traffic we're getting cross-region routing -> extra latency + egress billing. Customer is hitting rate limits and sometimes auth tokens are validated against the wrong auth cluster which returns 401s intermittently.

sre-alex: Mitigation options: 
- immediate: add a header rewrite rule at the edge to prefer client-provided `x-region-hint` (config change, no rollout)
- rollback: revert the canary to v3.11.7 for the affected pools (will require a rollback rollout)
- medium: patch header-merge filter to prefer client-supplied region header and add unit/integration tests.

devin: For quick mitigation I've deployed a temporary route config to the EU edge that injects `x-region-hint: eu-central-1` into upstream when incoming `:authority` matches `eu.*` — canary at 08:10UTC.

mara: After that change customer reports latencies back to normal and 503s decreased. They still see a small % of requests routed to us-west when concurrent bursts hit 50+ QPS.

support-lev: Billing team flagged ~€1.2k unexpected egress for the last 12h from that tenant due to cross-region traffic. We should queue a billing adjustment/credit while this is being fixed.

tzhao: I dove into the filter code: the bug is in header_merge.cc line 178 — when `proxy_regions.size()>0` we take `proxy_regions.front()` without checking if `client_region` exists. Patch incoming in PR #4897. Tests added to cover merge priority.

ops-bot: PR created: #4897 by tzhao -> header-merge: prefer client region over internal proxy region. CI: running.

sre-alex: Action items: 1) rollback canary to v3.11.7 in EU pools if we see >1% misroute after mitigation window ends (ETA 30m) 2) merge PR #4897 + release v3.12.1 with tests 3) billing credit for ACME customer (support-lev) 4) add an integration test to postman/regression harness to verify `x-region-hint` preservation across the L7 proxy 5) postmortem doc.

mara: I'll keep the thread updated. Thanks for quick response. :thumbsup:

devin: ETA for PR review + patch release ~2h. I’ll open a rollback if the canary progresses unexpectedly.

sre-alex: tagging oncall to monitor: @sre-oncall.

ops-bot: Monitoring alert created: region-misroute-rate (support): threshold=0.5% -> firing at 2026-03-17T08:11:00Z.

mara: Customer confirmed recovery for now. We'll follow up with a formal RCA and the update to the billing team.
